questions.title: Queue Reversal Via a Stack
questions.description:
The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int[] reversedQueue(int[] a)

Enqueue every value into a queue, then move them into a stack and pop them back out. Return the resulting order — the stack reverses the queue.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n.
Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line with the values after the queue-to-stack round trip, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000
-1000 <= a[i] <= 1000

questions.title: FIFO Serving Order
questions.description:
The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int[] servedOrder(int[] a)

Enqueue every value into a queue, then dequeue everyone. Return the serving order — for a queue it is exactly the arrival order (FIFO).

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n.
Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line with the serving order, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000
-1000 <= a[i] <= 1000

questions.title: Sum of First K Dequeued
questions.description:
The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static long sumDequeued(int[] a, int k)

Enqueue all values, then dequeue k of them and return their sum (k never exceeds n).

Input Format:
Line 1: integers n and k.
Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line: the sum of the first k dequeued values.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000
0 <= k <= n
-1000 <= a[i] <= 1000

questions.title: Deque Shuffle
questions.description:
The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int[] dequeShuffle(int[] a)

Process the values left to right: values at even indexes go to the back of a deque, values at odd indexes go to the front. Return the deque from front to back.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n.
Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line with the deque contents front to back, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000
-1000 <= a[i] <= 1000

questions.title: Sliding Window Sums
questions.description:
The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static long[] windowSums(int[] a, int k)

Return the sum of every window of k consecutive values (there are n - k + 1 windows).

Input Format:
Line 1: integers n and k.
Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line with the window sums, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= k <= n <= 1000
-10000 <= a[i] <= 10000

questions.title: Rotate a Queue
questions.description:
The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int[] rotatedQueue(int[] a, int k)

Rotate the queue left by k positions: dequeue the first k values and enqueue them at the back. Return the queue from front to rear.

Input Format:
Line 1: integers n and k.
Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line with the rotated queue, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000
0 <= k < n
-1000 <= a[i] <= 1000

questions.title: Printer Job Queue
questions.description:
An office printer serves jobs in arrival order within its paper budget: a job is printed (consuming its pages) only if enough paper remains, otherwise it is dropped without consuming anything.

The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int printedJobs(int[] pages, int budget)

Serve the jobs FIFO. Count how many jobs get printed.

Input Format:
Line 1: integers n and budget.
Line 2: n space-separated page counts.

Output Format:
One line: the number of printed jobs.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000
1 <= budget <= 100000
1 <= pages[i] <= 10000

questions.title: Supermarket Express Lane
questions.description:
A supermarket splits arriving shoppers into two lanes: five or fewer items go express, the rest go normal. Each lane preserves arrival order.

The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int[] laneSplit(int[] items)

Return the item counts in express-lane arrival order followed by normal-lane arrival order.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n.
Line 2: n space-separated item counts.

Output Format:
One line with the express lane counts then the normal lane counts, space-separated (in that order).

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000
1 <= items[i] <= 100

questions.title: Musical Chairs Elimination
questions.description:
Children stand in a circle; counting goes around and every k-th child leaves. A queue models the circle: pass the counted children to the back, remove the k-th.

The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int[] eliminationOrder(int[] people, int k)

Given the children in circle order and the count k, return the order in which they are eliminated. Counting restarts from the next child after each elimination; the child reached by the k-th count is removed.

Input Format:
Line 1: integers n and k.
Line 2: n space-separated child ids.

Output Format:
One line with the elimination order, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100
1 <= k <= 100
1 <= people[i] <= 1000

questions.title: First Unique Support Ticket
questions.description:
A support dashboard watches tickets arrive and wants the first ticket type that has not been seen twice.

The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int firstUniqueTicket(int[] a)

Return the first value (in arrival order) that occurs exactly once in the whole array, or -1 if every value repeats.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n.
Line 2: n space-separated ticket type ids.

Output Format:
One line: the first unique ticket type or -1.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000
1 <= a[i] <= 100

questions.title: Circular Queue Ring Buffer
questions.description:
A keyboard driver keeps keystrokes in a fixed-capacity ring buffer backed by a plain int array. You must implement it from scratch — no ArrayDeque or LinkedList allowed.

The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write exactly these three static methods:

    static void initQueue(int capacity)
    static int enqueue(int v)
    static int dequeue()

initQueue allocates the ring buffer for the given capacity (called once, first). enqueue stores v if there is room and returns 1, or returns 0 when the buffer is full. dequeue removes and returns the oldest value, or returns -1 when the buffer is empty. Use modular arithmetic on the array — the buffer must reuse freed slots.

Input Format:
Line 1: the capacity C.
Line 2: the number of operations m.
Next m lines: either "e x" (enqueue x) or "d" (dequeue).

Output Format:
One line per operation: enqueue prints 1 (success) or 0 (full); dequeue prints the value or -1 (empty).

Constraints:
1 <= C <= 1000
1 <= m <= 1000
-10000 <= x <= 10000

questions.title: Reverse First K of a Queue
questions.description:
A print spooler bumps the first k jobs to the back after reversing them. Standard technique: dequeue the first k into a stack, then re-queue.

The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int[] reverseFirstK(int[] a, int k)

Reverse the first k elements of the queue and keep the rest in order. Return the queue from front to rear.

Input Format:
Line 1: integers n and k.
Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line with the resulting queue, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= k <= n <= 1000
-1000 <= a[i] <= 1000

questions.title: Binary Numbers via a Queue
questions.description:
A number-formatter gadget generates the binary representations of 1..n with a queue of unfinished strings: every dequeued prefix spawns two longer prefixes.

The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static String[] binaryNumbers(int n)

Generate the binary strings for 1 to n in ascending order using a queue (start from "1"; dequeuing "x" enqueues "x0" and "x1"). Do not use Integer.toBinaryString.

Input Format:
One line: integer n.

Output Format:
One line with the n binary strings, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 500

questions.title: Interleave Queue Halves
questions.description:
A shuffle machine interleaves the two halves of a playlist queue: first song, then the song at the middle, then the second, and so on.

The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int[] interleaveHalves(int[] a)

n is even. Split the queue into front and back halves, then interleave them starting with the front half. Return the new queue from front to rear.

Input Format:
Line 1: even integer n.
Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line with the interleaved queue, space-separated.

Constraints:
2 <= n <= 1000 (n even)
-1000 <= a[i] <= 1000

questions.title: Moving Average Window
questions.description:
A load monitor reports the average load over the last k samples after each new sample arrives. A queue holds the current window.

The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int[] movingAverages(int[] samples, int k)

After each index i >= k - 1 report the integer division of the window sum by k. Return all the averages.

Input Format:
Line 1: integers n and k.
Line 2: n space-separated samples.

Output Format:
One line with n - k + 1 averages, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= k <= n <= 2000
0 <= samples[i] <= 1000

questions.title: Palindrome via Deque
questions.description:
A text tool checks words with both ends of a deque at once: compare the first and last characters, pop both, repeat.

The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int isPalindromeDeque(String s)

Load every character into a deque, then repeatedly compare and remove both ends. Return 1 if s reads the same both ways, else 0. Do not use StringBuilder or reverse helpers.

Input Format:
One line: the word s.

Output Format:
One line: 1 or 0.

Constraints:
1 <= s.length <= 1000
s contains lowercase letters

questions.title: Sliding Window Maximum
questions.description:
A traffic sensor reports the heaviest 5-minute load in every window: the maximum of each k-length window of the stream. A monotonic deque answers every window in O(1) amortized.

The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int[] slidingMax(int[] a, int k)

Return the maximum of every window of k consecutive values.

Input Format:
Line 1: integers n and k.
Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line with n - k + 1 maxima, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= k <= n <= 3000
-100000 <= a[i] <= 100000

questions.title: First Non-Repeating in a Stream
questions.description:
A live chat shows, after every message, the first character of the running text that has appeared exactly once so far — or a dash when every character repeats.

The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static String firstUniqueStream(String s)

After each prefix of s (length 1, 2, ... n) determine the first non-repeating character of that prefix, or '-' if none. Return the n results concatenated into one string. Count with an int[26]; use a queue of candidates — do not use HashMap.

Input Format:
One line: the stream s.

Output Format:
One line: n characters (first unique per prefix or '-').

Constraints:
1 <= s.length <= 1000
s contains lowercase letters

questions.title: Sliding Window Minimum
questions.description:
A cooling system reports the lowest temperature of every k-sample window using a monotonic deque that keeps candidates in increasing order.

The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int[] slidingMin(int[] a, int k)

Return the minimum of every window of k consecutive values.

Input Format:
Line 1: integers n and k.
Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line with n - k + 1 minima, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= k <= n <= 3000
-100000 <= a[i] <= 100000

questions.title: Minimum K-Consecutive Bit Flips
questions.description:
A conveyor controller can flip any window of exactly k consecutive bits at a time. Find the minimum number of flips to make every bit 1 — or report that it is impossible.

The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int minBitFlips(int[] a, int k)

a contains 0s and 1s. Each move flips a[i..i+k-1] for some i with i + k <= n. Return the minimum number of moves to turn every bit into 1, or -1 if impossible. Track flip effects with a queue of active flip end positions.

Input Format:
Line 1: integers n and k.
Line 2: n space-separated bits (0 or 1).

Output Format:
One line: minimum flips or -1.

Constraints:
1 <= k <= n <= 10000
a[i] is 0 or 1
